To find which two consecutive whole numbers $\sqrt[3]{30}$ lies between, we first identify the perfect cubes that are just below and just above $30.$

The perfect cubes closest to $30$ are $27$ and $64.$ We have

$$
27<30<64.
$$

Taking the cube root of each number, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{27} & <\sqrt[3]{30}<\sqrt[3]{64} \\ 3 & <\sqrt[3]{30}<4.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14185481/assets/3efc92b2664e8fade27edc67f977d78b317e73343d3201ac38c1fad807cdb01a.png)

This means that $\sqrt[3]{30}$ lies between the consecutive whole numbers $3$ and $4.$ 

Therefore, since $a<b,$ we have $a=3$ and $b=4.$
